contract: A task branch's PARENT - the branch its work merges into - as bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh emits it on a fm-fleet-snapshot.v1 task row. Each case is one state/<id>.meta written as lines in producer order; expect is the pair of task-row fields that meta must produce. base is the branch bin/fm-spawn.sh --base declared at launch; pr_base is the PR's own base ref, recorded by bin/fm-pr-check.sh from the forge and refreshed on every rerun. Both fields are always present, both are strings, and both are the empty string when unknown - never null, and never collapsed into one field: the consumer decides precedence (pr_base wins when both are set, because a PR's base is the live answer and a restack moves it), and it must be able to tell 'this task has no PR yet' apart from 'this task declared no base'. A branch whose parent is the repository's default branch is a top-level workstream on the board side, which is why an empty pair is a real answer rather than a gap to fill from the network. peer records what the logbook board's workstream tree does with each pair.
peer_implementation: logbook connector workstream tree (logbook item logbook-workstream-tree-w1), built against this file 2026-09-07; no case has been observed against a released peer yet, so every peer status here is 'planned' rather than a recorded observation.

peer.note: a task launched before --base existed, with no PR yet: the board leaves it top level rather than guessing
the working-branch case: the only parent known before a PR exists
a slashed branch name is one value, not a path to split
a task launched without a declared base that later opened a PR; pr_base= must not be read as base=
the ordinary shape once a PR exists: both agree and precedence is unobservable
the case precedence exists for: the PR was retargeted onto another branch after launch, so the board parents this branch under feature/stack-1 and keeps base as the stale declared value
a GitLab merge request records no base, exactly as it records no head; the declared base is what the board falls back to
a secondmate is a firstmate home rather than a branch; --base is refused on that spawn, so the pair is always empty and the board shows no workstream for it
